Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Chadian law does not provide a mandatory data breach notification protocol (noted explicitly in DLA Piper's Chad summary). Evidence: [DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Chad](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=TD).
revision_notes: Fetched the DLA Piper Chad law summary plus the dedicated breach-notification sub-page. The latter states explicitly: "No mandatory breach notification protocol is provided under Chadian law." Chad's data protection regime rests on Act No. 007/PR/2015 on Personal Data Protection and its 2019 implementing decree, enforced by ANSICE (established under Act No. 006/PR/2015) with administrative sanctions (warnings, processing bans, fines) and, via the Criminal Code, judicially imposed fines and imprisonment for breaches of the Act generally. None of these instruments impose a specific duty to notify users, regulators, or the data protection authority of a breach within a defined timeframe. A cross-check against dataguidance.com corroborates that the law does not require breach notification. Value Code 1 (No) is confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Chad has no statutory requirement obliging payment service providers, or any other data controller, to notify users, regulators or the data protection authority of data breaches, cybersecurity incidents or unauthorised access. The data protection regime rests on Act No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data and its 2019 implementing decree, enforced by the National Agency for Computer Security and Electronic Certification (ANSICE) through administrative sanctions such as warnings, processing bans and fines, and by the courts through criminal penalties of between one and five years' imprisonment and fines of XAF 1-10 million for breaches of the Act. Neither instrument establishes a mandatory breach notification protocol.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022 reports that for CEMAC (which includes Chad), "none of the countries in the CEMAC region have a national IPS"; Chad is not listed among domestic IPS systems live as of June 2022, but Chad participates in the regional interoperable retail payment switch GIMACPAY (launched July 2020) that provides domestic + cross-border instant clearing across CEMAC. Evidence: [AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022 report](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/EN_SIIPS_Report_web.pdf); [AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 CEMAC case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf)
revision_notes: Fetched the AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 CEMAC case study, GIMAC's own site and member directory, BEAC's payment-systems page, and a Launch Base Africa report (29 April 2026) drawing on BEAC's 2024 annual report. These confirm GIMACPAY is a regional (not Chad-specific) interoperable instant payment platform for cards, mobile money and transfers, commercially launched in July 2020 and operated by GIMAC under BEAC. By 2025 GIMAC's own figures put cumulative transaction value over FCFA 600 billion, while BEAC's 2024 annual report recorded 16,972 GIMACPAY transactions worth 726.97 billion FCFA (c.$1.31bn) region-wide, up 33.5% on 2023's 12,716 transactions/640.61 billion FCFA - still a small fraction of the c.18 million transactions worth FCFA 21.68 trillion processed by SYSTAC, the broader BEAC retail clearing system, in the same year. Chadian institutions are confirmed as active GIMACPAY participants (Moov Africa Tchad, Airtel Tchad, Banque Commerciale du Chari, Banque de l'Habitat Tchad, among others, connected since at least 2021), but no source gives Chad-specific coverage, participation-rate or transaction-share figures, and no domestic (Chad-only) IPS exists outside this regional infrastructure - consistent with AfricaNenda's finding that no CEMAC country runs a national IPS. This rules out the maximum code (5 = Fully deployed nationwide); the evidence supports the original Value Code of 4 (Partially deployed), which is confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Chad does not operate a stand-alone domestic instant payment system, but participates in GIMACPAY, the CEMAC-wide interoperable instant payment platform operated by the Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale (GIMAC) under the regional central bank, Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC). Commercially launched in July 2020, GIMACPAY enables near-instant card, mobile money and transfer payments both domestically and across the six-country CEMAC zone, and connects Chadian institutions including Moov Africa Tchad, Airtel Tchad, Banque Commerciale du Chari and Banque de l'Habitat Tchad. According to BEAC's 2024 annual report, GIMACPAY processed 16,972 transactions worth 726.97 billion CFA francs (around $1.31 billion) region-wide in 2024, a 33.5% increase on 2023, though this remains a small share of the region's total retail payment volumes, which stay heavily cash- and cheque-based via the SYSTAC clearing system. No Chad-specific coverage data is published, and deployment sits at a partial rather than fully nationwide stage.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: World Bank PAD for Chad Digital Transformation Project states "Only 0.1 percent of adults receive government payments in digital form," indicating extremely low digitization of government payments. Evidence: [World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project (P180000) PAD](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102502282341480/pdf/P180000048eed6040a13200ddaf8abe650.pdf).
revision_notes: Fetched the World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project (P180000) Project Information Document (Feb 2023), which states verbatim: "Only 0.1 percent of adults receive government payments in digital form." A related, more detailed World Bank project document repeats a figure of 3.6 percent of adults receiving government payments in digital form (based on 2021 Global Findex data) and separately notes that 15 percent of adults received a government payment of any kind (cash or digital) in 2022, driven mainly by social safety net transfers. Whichever specific estimate is used (0.1%-3.6% digitised), the figure sits well below the 20% threshold for the scale's lowest band. No more recent or materially higher estimate was found; a new World Bank-financed Adaptive and Productive Social Safety Nets Project (approved September 2024, running 2025-2030) is expanding a digital payment platform for social transfers but has not yet published an updated digitisation percentage. Value Code 1 (<20%) is confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Digitisation of government-to-person payments in Chad remains very low. World Bank project documentation for the Chad Digital Transformation Project records that only around 0.1-3.6% of adults receive government payments (salaries, pensions, social transfers) in digital form, based on 2021 Global Findex data, against 15% of adults who received a government payment in any form (cash or digital) in 2022, driven mainly by social safety net transfers. Government use of digital payment channels is limited to a few use cases, such as community teacher salaries and mobile money transfers for some social protection programmes outside the main cities, reflecting the absence of shared government digital payments infrastructure, an outdated legal framework and limited interoperability among mobile money providers. A World Bank-financed Adaptive and Productive Social Safety Nets Project, approved in 2024 and running to 2030, is developing a digital payment platform intended to expand digitised social transfers, but implementation remains at an early stage.
